2.1: A candidate showers a town with promises, handshakes and personal visits.
2.2: A politician attends your fundraiser and visits the hospital, so disagreeing feels like ingratitude.
2.3: A candidate promises to fix healthcare, education, infrastructure and wages, and none of it arrives.
2.4: A disengaged citizen is told their country needs them and is pulled back through patriotic guilt.
2.5: A constituent courted during the campaign is ignored after the election, calls unanswered.
2.6: A politician denies saying what they said, despite video evidence and transcripts.
2.7: A citizen is told to participate, then labeled radical for protesting and apathetic for not.
2.8: A politician is accessible one week and unreachable the next, rewarding loyalty unpredictably.
2.9: A government promises to release documents when the investigation concludes, and it never does.
2.10: A politician answers every question without answering anything, so the voter feels heard.
2.11: A corrupt politician accuses their opponent of corruption, and the accusation lands first.
2.12: A politician caught lying attacks the journalist who reported the lie.
2.13: A politician's first lie on camera is a scandal, the fifth is Tuesday.
2.14: A whistleblower is isolated from colleagues, put on leave and made professionally radioactive.
2.15: A politician tells each faction what it wants to hear, promising contradictory things.
2.16: Operatives discredit opponents through leaked documents, planted stories and anonymous tips.
2.17: Old photographs and out-of-context quotes are leaked before elections to destroy a reputation.
2.18: FOIA requests are denied and "no comment" becomes the official position on everything.
2.19: You get two options in every election, both preselected and pre-funded before you vote.
2.20: Citizens bond with a leader through shared crisis, and the leader gets credit for weathering it.
2.21: A citizen who voted, protested and called their representative stops participating.
2.22: An official says "this is for your safety" while monitoring your communications.
2.23: A citizen who asks too many questions is told to leave it to the experts.
2.24: Political opponents are stripped of reputation, career and family privacy until unrecognizable.
2.25: A leader says "God has a plan for this nation" to sidestep accountability.
2.26: Campaign donors get access and favorable policy while citizens without money are locked out.
2.27: An opponent's minor mistake is inflated into an existential threat.
2.28: Loyal staff are fired once inconvenient, years of service erased in a press release.
2.29: A new loyalist is installed immediately, with no mourning period and no transition.
2.30: The harm passes through a staffer, committee, agency and contractor, so no one is responsible.

4.1: A teacher tells a child they are gifted, and the child's sense of self attaches to that approval.
4.2: A scholarship demands a GPA that sacrifices your health, sleep and social life.
4.3: A child is told to study hard now because it will pay off later, with no guarantee.
4.4: A dropout is told to come back and finish, pulled in by guilt and sunk cost.
4.5: A child told they are special is ranked and scored, worth distilled into a number.
4.6: A struggling student is told they are not trying hard enough, when no one taught them how.
4.7: A student is told to think critically, then punished when the thinking challenges the curriculum.
4.8: Grades arrive unpredictably, an A for work barely tried and a C for work poured into.
4.9: A bachelor's degree was enough, then a master's, a doctorate, a post-doc, and the finish line retreats.
4.10: Teacher feedback says "needs improvement" without saying what or how it will be measured.
4.11: A teacher who cannot manage a classroom blames the students for being unmanageable.
4.12: A student who reports bullying is told to toughen up and develop thicker skin.
4.13: On the first day of school, a child is separated from their parent and told to sit still for hours.
4.14: A gifted child is pulled from peers into a separate track, and separate becomes lonely.
4.15: A teacher plays students against each other with class rank and grading curves.
4.16: Other students police each other's behavior, appearance and questions so the teacher doesn't have to.
4.17: A student who challenges authority is labeled troubled, oppositional and defiant in permanent records.
4.18: A student's emotional needs are met with "this is a classroom, not a therapy session."
4.19: A child "consents" to school by attending, though attendance is compulsory.
4.20: Students bond over all-nighters, exam anxiety and impossible deadlines.
4.21: A student who asked questions and was shut down stops raising their hand.
4.22: A teacher who restricts a child's movement and speech frames every restriction as care.
4.23: A twelve-year-old must raise a hand to use the bathroom.
4.24: A child's creativity and curiosity are replaced with compliance and memorization.
4.25: A struggling student is told everything happens for a reason.
4.26: A child is denied a school lunch because of an unpaid balance.
4.27: Pop quizzes and timed exams manufacture anxiety, training the child to associate learning with threat.
4.28: Students who fidget, question or feel too much are expelled, suspended, medicated or pushed out.
4.29: A student who withdrew is replaced by the next enrollment before the paperwork is processed.
4.30: A teacher who humiliated a student says they were speaking generally, not to anyone specifically.

6.1: An envelope says you are pre-approved, though a machine scanned your credit file.
6.2: A bank offers free checking and a sign-up bonus, then the fees activate twelve months later.
6.3: An advisor says "invest now and retire wealthy" and has moved firms by the time you retire.
6.4: A bank you left sends a letter saying it wants you back, with a special rate.
6.5: After one late payment, a pre-approved person is reclassified as high risk and charged more.
6.6: A customer calling about a fee is told it is in the forty-seven pages of terms and conditions.
6.7: A worker who asks for a raise is labeled ungrateful, and one who accepts is underpaid.
6.8: The stock market works like a slot machine, random wins keeping you investing through losses.
6.9: The credit score you needed last year is no longer enough this year.
6.10: Terms say "rates may vary" and "subject to change," a license to adjust after you commit.
6.11: A bank that charged hidden fees calls the customer irresponsible.
6.12: A customer who complains about hidden fees is told they should have read the contract.
6.13: A statement showing three hundred dollars of interest angers you at first, the twelfth does not.
6.14: Financial shame keeps people hiding debt from partners and struggles from friends.
6.15: A bank says another institution would charge you more, though all lead to the same extraction.
6.16: Collection agencies you never borrowed from call to harass you over debts the lender gave up on.
6.17: A single financial crisis leaves a bad credit score that follows you for seven years.
6.18: An insurance claim is denied with no explanation, and calls loop through menus and transfers.
6.19: You sign loan documents at peak emotional investment, formatted to discourage reading.
6.20: A worker says "I can't leave this job, I need the benefits," bonded to their employer.
6.21: A person denied loans and buried in debt eventually stops trying to build stability.
6.22: An advisor says "let me handle this for you, it's too complex for most people."
6.23: A bank asks "are you sure you want to withdraw that amount?" about your own money.
6.24: At every gathering the first question is "what do you do," and net worth becomes self-worth.
6.25: A person struggling financially is told money isn't everything.
6.26: Debt works as a leash, because leaving means default and losing the house and car.
6.27: A bank processes the largest transaction first so the smaller ones bounce, generating multiple fees.
6.28: In foreclosure, the bank takes the house, keeps every payment and knows only your loan number.
6.29: A new borrower fills your slot the next business day on identical terms.
6.30: A bank says its processing order is not designed to maximize fees.

9.1: An interrogation begins with warmth, and by the time you see it was strategic, the recording is running.
9.2: A public defender is free but carries eighty other cases and can give you twelve minutes.
9.3: A prosecutor offers a good word with the judge, a promise with no guarantee of delivery.
9.4: A missed appointment or failed drug test pulls a person back into the system.
9.5: An arrested person has their name published and mugshot released to the press before trial.
9.6: The confession is called voluntary when it was coerced, and the record reads as just.
9.7: The accused must accept two years for something they may not have done or risk twenty at trial.
9.8: A parolee is released, but the release can be revoked at any time, the door propped open.
9.9: A probationer who met every requirement finds new requirements and an extended timeline.
9.10: An officer says "things will go easier for you if you cooperate," promising nothing.
9.11: An officer who used excessive force charges the victim with resisting arrest.
9.12: A victim of police brutality is arrested and charged while the officer files the official report.
9.13: A metal detector at a courthouse feels wrong the first time, and then you stop noticing.
9.14: A human being is placed in a concrete box for twenty-three hours a day, and it is called housing.
9.15: A prosecutor says your friend is talking, so talk first or take the heavier sentence.
9.16: Informants gather information on friends, family and neighbors for reduced charges or payments.
9.17: An arrest record is published online before conviction, and the exoneration is whispered.
9.18: A public defender doesn't return calls while the client waits in a cell for months.
9.19: A defendant takes the plea because risking greater punishment at trial makes it the rational choice.
9.20: A parolee calls their parole officer "one of the good ones," bonding with the source of power.
9.21: A person arrested, plea-bargained, incarcerated and re-arrested stops believing the system can be just.
9.22: A probation officer who dictates your schedule says "this is for your reintegration."
9.23: An incarcerated person is told when to eat, sleep, exercise, what to wear and who to speak to.
9.24: The inmate number replaces the name, and the number is who you are now.
9.25: A crime victim is told to "forgive and heal" before the system attempts justice.
9.26: With cash bail, the person who can pay goes home tonight and the one who cannot sits in a cell.
9.27: A warrant is issued for a minor technical violation specifically to justify a search.
9.28: A person released from prison walks out with a bus ticket, a box of belongings and no plan.
9.29: A new inmate fills the bed the same day, and the mattress is not cold.
9.30: An officer who used excessive force says "I feared for my life."

11.1: A recruiter builds rapport and offers belonging to young people who have never been offered it.
11.2: The military offers tuition, housing, healthcare and a signing bonus, all conditional on years of service.
11.3: A recruiter promises a seventeen-year-old a trade and travel the military has no obligation to deliver.
11.4: A veteran gets re-enlistment calls timed to when civilian life feels most disorienting.
11.5: A soldier praised during recruitment becomes a unit, a body, a resource allocated to a mission.
11.6: A soldier who witnessed an atrocity is told it didn't happen the way they remember.
11.7: A soldier must follow an order they believe is wrong or refuse and face court-martial.
11.8: A soldier is praised by one superior and punished by another for the same action.
11.9: A six-month deployment stretches to twelve, then eighteen, and the family hears just a little longer.
11.10: A recruiter promises "great career opportunities" and "paths to advancement," committing to nothing.
11.11: A commanding officer whose failures caused a disaster blames the soldiers on the ground.
11.12: A soldier who reports sexual assault is investigated more thoroughly than the person reported.
11.13: The first time a soldier takes a life it changes something, and the tenth time is operational.
11.14: A recruit is removed from family and community, so they have no leverage inside the institution.
11.15: The military pits Army against Marines and Navy against Air Force, calling it tradition.
11.16: Fellow soldiers tell a struggling member to suck it up and not make them look bad.
11.17: A soldier who reports war crimes is labeled a traitor, a coward and a disgrace to the uniform.
11.18: A veteran who filed a disability claim waits months and years while paperwork is lost.
11.19: An enlistee "volunteers" under limited options, aggressive recruitment and economic pressure.
11.20: A damaged veteran defends the military because attacking it betrays the people they survived with.
11.21: A veteran denied and delayed on a VA claim eventually stops filing.
11.22: A commanding officer says "this is for your own good" and "this is how we keep you alive."
11.23: A recruit is told when to wake, eat and sleep, what to wear, how to stand and how to think.
11.24: In basic training, the name is replaced by a rank, the clothes by a uniform, the hairstyle erased.
11.25: A veteran in pain is told "you served your country, you should be proud."
11.26: Enlistment bonuses and tuition benefits vest over time and are forfeited if the soldier leaves.
11.27: A briefing says the enemy is closing in and the attack is imminent, demanding immediate compliance.
11.28: A discharged veteran is handed a DD-214, a list of phone numbers, a handshake and a bus ticket.
11.29: A new recruit fills the slot before the discharge paperwork is filed, same bunk, different body.
11.30: An officer whose order killed civilians says "I followed the rules of engagement."

13.1: A teacher finds you at your most wounded and says "you're one of the ones who can feel it."
13.2: The first session is free, opening a wound the paid program promises to close.
13.3: A practitioner says "you're almost there, one more intensive and you'll feel the shift."
13.4: A teacher you tried to leave writes "I've been thinking about you."
13.5: A practitioner who said you're not broken now says "I can feel the resistance in your field."
13.6: You say the practice isn't working and are told feeling worse is the healing crisis.
13.7: A student is told to trust their intuition, then corrected whenever it contradicts the teacher.
13.8: One ceremony cracks you open and the next produces nothing but nausea and confusion.
13.9: You complete the program and are told there is a deeper layer, the ancestral field.
13.10: A practitioner senses "an entity attachment in the left shoulder," which cannot be checked.
13.11: A controlling guru tells the student "what you're seeing in me is your own shadow."
13.12: A client who says they don't feel safe in this container is told that is what to work with.
13.13: Your trauma is called a "soul contract," strange the first time and normal by the tenth.
13.14: A teacher says "your old friends are at a different frequency."
13.15: A guru says "most people move through this phase faster," comparing you to other students.
13.16: Other students tell you "the discomfort is the medicine," enforcing the teacher's narrative.
13.17: A student who leaves is said to have let their ego win and chosen comfort over growth.
13.18: A teacher warm during the paid program becomes unreachable the moment it ends.
13.19: A ceremony opens with "by staying in this space you are consenting to whatever arises."
13.20: A cathartic ceremony bonds you to the facilitator like a trauma survivor to their rescuer.
13.21: A seeker who has tried every modality and still carries the wound begins to believe they are the problem.
13.22: A practitioner tells you what to eat, when to sleep and who to see, calling it guidance.
13.23: A practitioner tells the client "you're not ready to hold that truth yet."
13.24: A wellness seeker adopts a new name, diet, vocabulary and wardrobe, replacing who they were.
13.25: You say you are angry and are told "anger is a lower vibration."
13.26: A practitioner says "scarcity mindset is blocking your abundance" about your financial boundary.
13.27: A practitioner says "there's an entity in your field that needs to be cleared immediately."
13.28: A client who stops paying stops existing in the practitioner's awareness, the warmth withdrawn.
13.29: A new client fills your spot the same week, because the schedule follows the practitioner's income.
13.30: A harmed client is told "I was only holding space, whatever came up was yours."
